incidents.vector: A malicious Chromium extension spoofed the Perplexity AI brand and a typosquatted domain, overriding the browser's default search provider to route every Omnibox query and keystroke-level search suggestion through attacker-controlled infrastructure before redirecting to legitimate search engines.
incidents.impact: The extension performed keystroke-level capture of search activity and shipped its own logging server code; Microsoft reported it to Google, which removed it. No credential theft was confirmed but the access granted elevated privacy and surveillance risk.

incidents.victim: Government officials, journalists, military and political figures (US, Europe, Ukraine)
incidents.attacker: Russia — FSB and military intelligence services
incidents.vector: Russian intelligence actors impersonated Signal and WhatsApp support accounts in social-engineering phishing, tricking high-value targets into surrendering verification codes, account PINs and—in evolved tactics—encrypted-messaging Backup Recovery Keys; some attacks altered legitimate Signal group invite pages to link attacker devices.
incidents.impact: Attackers compromised individual Signal and WhatsApp accounts (not the platforms' encryption), gaining access to message histories and group chats; stolen backup recovery keys remain valid even after account recreation. The US State Department posted a $10 million Rewards for Justice bounty on the groups tracked as UNC5792 and UNC4221.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian government/military and entities tied to Italian foreign policy
incidents.vector: Russia's Turla group deployed STOCKSTAY, a modular .NET backdoor that masquerades as a stock-market or PDF/calculator utility and communicates with command-and-control over encrypted WebSocket connections, supporting file theft, screen capture and command execution.
incidents.impact: Continued cyber-espionage collection against Ukrainian government and military targets and parties interested in Italian foreign policy; STOCKSTAY has been in active development since at least December 2022 and shares code with Turla's KAZUAR toolkit.

incidents.victim: Southeast Asian government agencies and state-owned energy infrastructure
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking actor CL-STA-1062 (overlapping with UAT-7237) exploited web applications to drop ASPX web shells, then used SoftEther VPN, Mimikatz, JuicyPotato and a new bespoke .NET backdoor 'TinyRCT' disguised as legitimate system files for command execution, credential theft and data exfiltration.
incidents.impact: At least ten Southeast Asian organizations were likely compromised between October and December 2025, including two state-owned critical energy infrastructure entities; attackers exfiltrated database contents and full web-server source code and conducted reconnaissance for lateral movement.

incidents.vector: After gaining initial access via rogue SD-WAN peering connections and manipulating default admin passwords, the actor exploited a zero-day privilege-escalation flaw (CVE-2026-20245) in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager via a malicious CSV tenant upload to add a root account, then ran anti-forensic cleanup scripts to erase its footprint.
incidents.impact: The attacker achieved root-level control of the centralized SD-WAN orchestrator at a service provider, exfiltrated SD-WAN fabric configurations and established stealthy persistent access to internal enterprise traffic; intrusion activity spanned late 2025 through April 2026.

incidents.victim: Transport for London; SSM Health and Sutter Health (US)
incidents.vector: Members of the Scattered Spider group used SIM-swapping and voice/SMS phishing to steal employee credentials and multi-factor codes, enabling network intrusions and extortion.
incidents.impact: Two UK members pleaded guilty on day one of trial to the August 2024 attack that crippled Transport for London and to hacking US healthcare providers SSM Health and Sutter Health; a related US indictment ties the group to 120 intrusions across 47 entities and at least $115 million in ransom payments.

incidents.vector: Tata Electronics confirmed a cyberattack after documents allegedly belonging to customers including Apple and Tesla surfaced online; the specific intrusion method was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Allegedly stolen customer-linked documents appeared publicly, indicating data theft and a likely extortion or leak scenario affecting a major contract electronics manufacturer and its high-profile customers.

incidents.victim: FortiGate firewall and VPN operators worldwide (~73,932 systems, 194 countries)
incidents.industry: Cross-sector (government, telecom, finance, healthcare, manufacturing, critical infrastructure)
incidents.vector: Threat actors conducted roughly 1.16 billion credential attempts against FortiGate devices (and ~2.1 billion against MSSQL servers), intercepted SSL VPN authentication hashes, cracked them on a 45-GPU cluster, and recovered plaintext admin/VPN credentials from exported configuration files for offline use against Active Directory environments.
incidents.impact: The 'FortiBleed' dataset exposes valid admin and SSL VPN credentials for ~73,932 FortiGate URLs across 21,600+ domains, independently validated as authentic; confirmed victims include a Turkish NATO defense contractor from which classified documents were allegedly exfiltrated. Many affected devices remained online and internet-exposed, and offline cracking left no logs of the initial theft.

incidents.victim: Consumers using Android-based TV streaming boxes (millions of devices)
incidents.vector: The 'Popa' component of the Vo1d/Badbox botnet ships pre-installed or bundled in pirated streaming apps on cheap Android TV boxes, enrolling the device's home internet connection into a residential-proxy network that maintains long-lived encrypted tunnels for relaying third-party traffic.
incidents.impact: Millions of consumer TV boxes were forced to relay internet traffic tied to advertising fraud, account takeovers and mass data-scraping (one event spread scraping across 1.4 million IP addresses); researchers linked the proxy infrastructure to NetNut, operated by publicly-traded Israeli firm Alarum Technologies, which disputed the 'botnet' characterization.

incidents.victim: North American academic, medical and military research institutions
incidents.vector: PRC-nexus actor UNC6508 exploited externally facing REDCap research-data servers (including legacy versions vulnerable to downgrade), deployed custom INFINITERED malware to harvest login credentials and persist through software upgrades, then pivoted to domain-admin accounts and abused Google Workspace content-compliance rules to silently BCC-forward sensitive emails to attacker accounts.
incidents.impact: The actor remained undetected for over a year (earliest compromise September 2023, activity through November 2025) while pursuing defense, AI, uncrewed-systems, cyber and medical research across multiple US and Canadian institutions; Google Threat Intelligence disrupted the infrastructure and notified affected organizations.
